_comment_record_hz: Section H's own last clause: 'If frame capture measurably distorts frame timing, the overhead note records it and the perf audit (X08) runs without capture.' It does, and it is measured: at 1920x1080 under this container's software rasteriser one readback+PNG encode costs 126.5 ms mean / 218.9 ms max, which at 0.5 Hz amortises to 1.054 ms/frame -- over the ~1 ms/frame line the protocol asks about. A perf audit that recorded frames would be corrupting the one number it exists to produce, so the continuous record is OFF for this segment alone. Set by the instrumentation lane from its own measurement, not a transcription choice. Every other segment keeps its record; at the 0.1 Hz journey baseline the same grab amortises to 0.21 ms/frame, comfortably under the line.
title: DIAG performance audit (protocol E.9)
_source: ralph/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md E.9, transcribed mechanically per ralph/GATE_F_INSTRUMENTATION_REQUEST.md section 6. Entry save per protocol B: 'any; teleport permitted'.
_diag: This is a DIAG segment. Every teleport step carries "diag": true, and protocol 0.6 travels with every number here: no pacing, navigation, difficulty or economy claim may ever be sourced from a DIAG segment.
_owner_only: E.9, verbatim: 'Explicitly recorded as [OWNER-ONLY], unverified: handheld frame rate, GPU frame time, VRAM, battery/thermal. The report states the CPU-shape numbers and the structural counts and stops there. No test in this protocol may output a "device FPS" number, because no honest one can exist here.' Nothing in this segment produces one, and SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md records that the harness has no code path that could.
_two_modes: E.9 asks for tools/perf_profile.gd at its six sites in BOTH modes: --headless for CPU frame/physics and directly-timed subsystem costs, and --mode=render under xvfb for draw calls/primitives. Those are separate invocations of a separate tool (instrumentation request section 10 forbids modifying it), not steps in this file; this segment's own contribution is the harness-side frame-time shape at the same six sites, taken through the same live world the journey ran in.

steps.title: what this segment is

args.text: E.9's performance audit, restricted to what is honestly measurable in this envelope: CPU frame/physics shape, directly-timed subsystem costs, draw calls and primitives under the render mode, placement/instance counts, and boot/save/load/transition durations.

steps.title: VOCABULARY GAP: this file cannot invoke tools/perf_profile.gd

args.text: E.9's first bullet is six sites x two modes of tools/perf_profile.gd with 'JSON output archived per site'. SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md's vocabulary drives the GAME; it has no action that launches a second Godot process or archives another tool's JSON, and instrumentation request section 10 explicitly forbids modifying perf_profile.gd. Those twelve runs therefore happen from tools/gate_f/run_segment.sh's own invocations, outside this step-script, and their JSON is archived beside this segment's telemetry. Named here so the run-end inventory check can see it was not silently dropped.

steps.expected: a note event carries this observation into events.jsonl

steps.title: VOCABULARY GAP: placement/instance counts have no assert check
